title: NILS model card
description: Record 42 (D15): what a registered model is, as the engine and Kvasir both read it. A model is identified by the digest of its canonical artifact, never by its name; the name and version are how people call it and are unique together. The card travels with the model from the job that fitted it to the registry and is kept whole. A reader keeps a key it does not know, so a later version can add one without breaking an older reader.

digest.description: sha256 of the bytes, lowercase hex, prefixed

kind.description: encoder: turns an image into features; head: answers a task from an encoder's features, and names its encoder; pass: a model the classifier runs as one of its passes; segmenter: writes a mask; served: a language model a gateway serves, which Kvasir registers (reserved in the engine)

slot.description: Where the model answers its task. Several admitted models may answer a task and slot, and the site chooses the one that does (record 55 D4). The engine takes site, the one site-wide model per task (record 42 R4), and cohort:<name>, a model of one cohort in a slot of its own; backend:<name> is Kvasir's, whose slot is the backend that serves the model

reference.description: Another registered model, by its digest

hardware.description: What it was measured on: the cores, the card, the storage

speed.description: One measured speed, in stacks a second

digest.description: The identity: the digest of the canonical artifact. For a head, a plain format (ONNX, or JSON coefficients) rather than a pickle, which executes code when it is loaded; for a served model, the weights file (a GGUF's sha256)

task.description: What the model answers, such as axis:body_part for a head that decides an axis of the pack, or chat for a served model

encoder.description: The encoder a head reads the features of. A head names its encoders here or in encoders, at least one: a new encoder makes its heads stale

parts.description: Record 55 E2: a cascade, one model that names its parts, each a registered model that is not retired, by digest, under the name of the pipeline input it fills (body part's encoder, head, coarse, student, deferral; post-contrast's student, fusion and arms, record 55 E3); a run of the cascade is given each part, and the cascade itself as its input cascade. Promoting the cascade retires none of its parts

encoders.description: Record 43: every encoder a head reads the features of, in the order it concatenates them, each registered before the head. An encoder given as well is one of them, and a card that names only encoder has that one

label_set.description: The digest of the label set the model was fitted on (labels.tsv, record 42 S7): one the registry wrote, or one registered from outside the engine with its rows keyed by DICOM identity (record 55 E6), and none holding items of a sealed certification sample, or the registration is refused (record 40 R3)

sealed.description: Whether the labels came from a random draw rather than from items a system chose to ask about

trained_on.description: The exact labels, as a digest, not prose

threshold.description: Record 43: the probability at or above which the model's proposal is staged as its decision, for a person to commit; below it a proposal is a review item only. Whoever runs the model may raise it for a run and never lower it. A card without one has every proposal asked as a review item

pack_version.description: The pack whose axis values a head was built for, such as mri@0.3.0

image_digest.description: The container image that runs the model, pinned by its manifest digest, when one does

metrics.description: What the fitting job measured, by name: accuracy, ece, brier, per-class counts and the like. Numbers, or objects of numbers; never a stack, a subject or an image

preprocessing.description: How an input is prepared before the model sees it, with a version, so that features made under another preparation are not mixed

runtime.description: The runtime a check was run under. A check pinned to a runtime says nothing about another

claim.description: What was measured, in words: the measure, the set and the reference

bound.description: Its bound, such as the one-sided exact 95 % lower bound, where the claim has one

evidence.description: The evidence run the number comes from

tested.description: Record 55 D4: the claims its study tested, each with its value, its bound and the evidence run it comes from

gpu.description: With a GPU; none only for a model whose gpu is none

speed.description: Record 55 A5: stacks a second on a CPU alone and with a GPU, each with the hardware it was measured on

gpu.description: What the model needs of a GPU: none, optional (it takes one when one is present and free, under the lease) or required

class.description: I, the same answer always; II, the same answer within the tolerance on the model's score; III, every change is between an answer and not sure

tolerance.description: For I and II, the largest calibrated probability difference allowed between the CPU and the GPU answers (0.001 for I where none is given); for III, the largest share of stacks whose answer changes between a value and not sure

set.description: The fixed equivalence set it was measured on

equivalence.description: Record 55 A5: the class of the difference between its CPU and GPU answers its study measured. The admission suite measures it again, and a model whose measured class is worse than this is not admitted. Not needed where gpu is none

lambda1.description: The least calibrated probability of System 1's answer

lambda2.description: The least reliability of the rules on the header

evidence.description: The run that chose them by Learn then Test

gate.description: Record 55 D3 (spec 11.2), a System 1 model's card (task system1): the review gate's thresholds per axis, chosen by Learn then Test on training-family damage and frozen with the model. On a dataset flagged as having damaged headers, the rules' answer is accepted where System 1's answer equals it, its probability is at least lambda1 and the rules' reliability is at least lambda2; the thresholds belong to the round of this model and a rules version
